log: A LEARNED TIE-BREAKER -- does set attention beat counting?
Headroom: truth is in the top tie group 48.8% of the time; hand-built tie-breakers claimed 31%
of it and the winner was raw frequency. 69% unclaimed.
GeoConv is NOT included: it needs a surface point cloud per entity, and a tie group is gene
names -- 311 structures against 5,282 catalysts, 5.9% coverage at best. Category error.
The transformer IS applicable: every hand-built tie-breaker scores candidates INDEPENDENTLY and
cannot condition on who else is in the group. Attention can. That is the mechanism under test.
PREDECLARED: beats freq AND its untrained control => set context is real. ~ logistic => a fitted
combination is what helps. ~ untrained => capacity does not, which a median group of 3 predicts.

trained 0.365+-0.013  untrained 0.315+-0.029  | 25/25 seed pairs favour trained | p=0.0040
READING
TRAINING DOES SOMETHING: 0.365 vs its random-init control 0.315 over 5 seeds
(p=0.0040). The listwise objective is learnable and the architecture is not inert.
BUT IT BUYS NOTHING OVER COUNTING. freq is 0.367 with ZERO parameters and logistic is
0.373 with ten; the 8,929-parameter transformer is 0.365, and the paired test cannot
separate it from freq (worst p=1.000) or logistic (worst p=0.804).
So attention learns a real function of these features, but everything it learns was already
reachable by a linear fit on the same five numbers. The set context is not the missing piece.
Likeliest reason: the median tie group is 3. There is almost nothing to
attend over, and only 315 groups are usable for training at all.
Headroom claimed at @1: freq 29% | logistic 32% | transformer 28% | untrained 0%
NOTE the untrained control sits at 0.315, well above the 0.314 random floor. A random
projection of features that already correlate with the answer is not a random ordering, which is
why 'better than random' was never the bar and the untrained arm is the one that matters.
